description: Saves one revision to one existing calendar feed owned by the connected account for a user-approved schedule change. Accepts one fixed-schema change set with up to 250 event changes and/or a feed title or description change; all stored calendar changes commit together in one transaction, or none are saved. The schema declares every supported change: add creates an event; update changes selected fields or uses reset_fields to restore saved field baselines; delete marks an existing event canceled without permanently erasing it; restore reinstates that same event and may update selected fields; feed_patch changes only the calendar title or description. No dynamic operation discovery, fetched schemas, arbitrary commands or arbitrary endpoints are supported. dry_run=true validates and previews the proposed change set without saving calendar changes, advancing the revision or spending credits. The response contains the exact before/after changes and any billing quote. User approval of that exact preview is a prerequisite for saving with dry_run=false. Saving requires the returned preview_receipt and the identical feed_id, expected_revision, request_id, operations and feed_patch. The receipt binds that validated preview, not user consent. Changed proposals or expired previews require a new preview and approval; revision conflicts require current feed data and a new preview. Omitted events and fields remain unchanged. Cancellation assessment from a revised schedule requires the complete unfiltered event set; unrelated events and manual fields remain unchanged unless explicitly included in the approved changes. Uncertain event matches require user clarification. Updates address matched event IDs; a duplicate add is not an update. A recurring-series target is series_id with scope=occurrence, following or series; occurrence/following uses the original scheduled occurrence_date, including moved occurrences. reset_fields can include cancellation to restore source cancellation policy. Entire-series edits include history and all returned segments are part of the preview. Explicit null in set clears nullable fields; reset_fields restores saved baselines. expected_revision prevents overwriting concurrent changes. An uncertain save is retried with the identical request_id and payload, including the original preview_receipt, rather than a new operation. Included editing access has no credit charge or credit-consent prompt. A quoted one-credit editing window requires explicit user authorization of the deduction and resulting balance before confirm_credit_charge=true; that authorization may be added after preview. Preview approval or an automation default does not authorize credit spending. publication.status reports calendar-file preparation, not subscription access. distribution_ready reports subscription availability at the returned revision; availability may change afterward. Preview proposals are recoverable for up to one hour; expired drafts are removed automatically. Previewing temporarily stores only the exact proposed calendar fields, without writing calendar events or advancing their revision. Returned feed_id and request_id identify that exact proposal for recovery. Recovery accepts only feed_id, the original request_id, dry_run=true and recover_preview=true. Reconstructed changes, guessed identifiers and latest-preview selection are unsupported. Recovery returns the original unexpired preview and exact save_arguments without extending expiry, saving or spending credits. Saving a recovered preview requires fresh user approval of its exact changes and the returned save_arguments unchanged; confirm_credit_charge remains false without explicit authorization of the current quoted charge. Recovery is not consent. Recovery with saved=true reports an already completed save and requires no additional save. An unavailable or expired proposal requires current feed data, a new request_id, a new preview and user approval; a changed proposal is a new approval decision. Scope is limited to the connected account’s Smart Calendars AI feeds. No mailbox access, source-document retrieval, automatic source monitoring, scheduled PDF checks or document refresh is provided. Structured schedule content is supplied explicitly by the caller. Result links: subscription_open_url is the exact HTTPS handoff to the default calendar app via webcal; subscription_options_url provides Apple/default, Google, Outlook and copy-link choices; subscription_url is the copyable HTTPS calendar-file fallback; manage_url opens the feed dashboard. URL hosts, paths and tokens identify the returned resource and are not interchangeable. A filtered_subscription has its own links for that selection; top-level links remain unfiltered. Subscription access requires distribution_ready=true. Opening a link does not confirm a subscription; confirmation occurs in the user’s calendar app.

confirm_credit_charge.description: True only for explicit user authorization of the current quoted credit deduction and resulting balance. Preview approval alone, a recovered receipt or an automation default does not authorize credit spending.

dry_run.description: True previews and validates the exact proposed changes without changing calendar events, advancing the revision or spending credits. The preview returns before/after changes, any billing quote and a preview_receipt. False saves the same proposal using its valid preview_receipt. The receipt proves preview integrity, not user approval; preview approval and any required credit authorization remain separate prerequisites. Defaults to false.

expected_revision.description: Last read feed revision; prevents overwriting concurrent edits.

feed_id.description: Identity of the selected calendar, as returned in feed results.

feed_patch.description: Proposed calendar title and/or description changes for this revision. Omitted fields stay unchanged.

description.description: Replacement short calendar description, or null to clear it. Conversation history and user-profile data are outside this field’s scope.

operations.description: Proposed event additions, updates, cancellations or restorations for this revision, with at most 250 operations. Saved operations and feed_patch commit together or none are saved.

event.description: Structured calendar fields for one event from the reviewed schedule.

assignee.description: Optional event assignee explicitly named in the schedule; not the connected account identity, email address or a user profile.

description.description: Event notes the user intends to publish with this calendar. Chat history, credentials, health records and unrelated personal context are outside this field’s scope.

end_date.description: Inclusive last calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. A bounded multi-day range represents one event unless the user requests separate events.

end_time.description: Local event end time in HH:mm format, on end_date when supplied or start_date otherwise. All-day events have no clock time.

facet_actors.description: Source-grounded participants or organizers (people, teams or organizations), not an invented audience such as everyone at a school. Source-derived labels use the existing facet vocabulary, spelling and language. Unchanged fields retain their tags.

facet_topic.description: Source-grounded stable category, not the full event title. Source-derived labels use the existing facet vocabulary, spelling and language. Unchanged fields retain their tags.

facet_venue.description: Source-grounded venue name. Source-derived labels use the existing facet vocabulary, spelling and language. Unchanged fields retain their tags.

is_all_day.description: True for an all-day calendar event with dates and no clock times; false for a timed event with a local start time and optional end time.

location.description: The event venue explicitly supplied in the schedule or requested correction, not the user’s current, home or device location. User geolocation is outside this field’s scope.

recurrence.description: Recurrence configuration, or null for a non-recurring event. An object represents repetition explicitly stated in the source or established by separately listed regular occurrences. A single bounded multi-day range is one occurrence with start_date/end_date. Recurrence objects require all schema fields with valid values; empty or partial objects are invalid.

endDate.description: End date for recurrence in YYYY-MM-DD format, or null if no end date

interval.description: Interval between recurrences (e.g., 2 for every 2 weeks)

monthlyType.description: Type of monthly recurrence: by date or by weekday pattern

occurrenceCount.description: Number of occurrences before ending, or null if no occurrence limit

selectedDaysOfMonth.description: Selected days of month (1-31, -1 for last day, -2 for second-last)

weekdayCategory.description: Category or specific weekday for monthly/yearly patterns

weekdayOrdinal.description: Ordinal position of weekday in month

start_date.description: Event start date in YYYY-MM-DD format, using the event timezone for timed events.

start_time.description: Local event start time in HH:mm format. All-day events have no clock time.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the event local dates and times, for example Europe/Berlin or UTC.

title.description: Event title from the supplied schedule.

external_key.description: Source-stable, namespaced event identity, for example school-a:session-104, retained when a title or date changes. A duplicate add does not update the event; updates address the existing event_id.

op.description: Adds a new event using the supplied event fields and optional source-stable external_key.

event_id.description: Identity of the existing event returned with the calendar event data. An event target is an alternative to series_id and scope.

occurrence_date.description: Original scheduled occurrence date in YYYY-MM-DD format for occurrence or following scope, including when the occurrence has moved.

op.description: Updates selected fields or resets selected overrides on an existing event or recurring-series target.

reset_fields.description: Selected overrides whose saved baselines are restored. A field without an override stays unchanged, including values supplied when adding the event. Explicit null in set clears a nullable field; reset_fields restores its baseline. The same field in both set and reset_fields is invalid.

scope.description: Extent of a series change: occurrence affects one occurrence, following affects that occurrence and later ones, and series affects the entire series including history.

series_id.description: Identity of the recurring series returned with the calendar event data. A series target is an alternative to event_id.

set.description: Only supplied fields change. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Explicit null clears a nullable field, for example {"location":null,"description":null}; it does not restore its baseline.

assignee.description: Optional event assignee explicitly named in the schedule; not the connected account identity, email address or a user profile.

recover_preview.description: Recovery of the exact unexpired preview by its original request_id. Requires only feed_id, the original request_id, dry_run=true and recover_preview=true; all other arguments are invalid. Recovery does not save, extend expiry or authorize a charge. request_id.description: Opaque, non-personal idempotency key for this operation. Identical retries retain the same key and payload to prevent duplicate changes. User identifiers, chat/session IDs, telemetry and personal data are outside this field’s scope.
